questions.answer: A bit confusing and painfully slow.

questions.answer: As little as possible. Mostly found information through fellow students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses available were diverse and were very interesting. Unfortunately, the fact that they were only 6 ECTS were disappointing since the time constraints led to a very surface level teaching. I want to point out that this was not due to fault of the professors, but rather a systematic problem. I was also a bit disappointed with the fact that the actual outcome was more intended to be memorization of facts rather than actual understanding and implementation of the material learned. This was very evident through the exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt like the level was rather low in most cases, but this I think was mostly due to the time constraint that led to surface level understanding of the material, especially in some of the literature classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my opinion it compared rather low, due to the aforementioned reasons. I feel like the teaching style at UCPH is more focused on fundamental understanding and applied knowledge, whereas the style of teaching at UAB almost exclusively focused on memorization of facts for the numerous multiple choice exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
106188 Theory of Democracy
106205 International Relations

106297 British Romantic Literature
106306 Literature of the United States III: From 1950 to the Present

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Relations and Theory of Democracy were highly interesting since it was part of a discipline I was not used to, and British Romantic Literature was also very professional and in-depth.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing. I didn't experience any costs that weren't expected. Housing, transportation, food, books, and cultural activities were the only things I ended up spending money on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: transportation was very cheap, food and cost of living was also cheap compared to home country, which was expected and planned for. I spent an extra amount of money food due to my interest and wish to try many different restaurants, but if a student was on a cheaper budget it would have been entirely possible to have lower living expenses than me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The opportunities for engagement in sports and clubs were very good, and the fellow students were very friendly and inclusive.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only signed up for the local gym and had a single days practice with the university rugby team. Unfortunately due to scheduling conflicts with my courses and rugby practice, it was rather difficult to do both and I chose to focus on the academic part of my exchange.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting involved in various campus activities to meet local students and create a social network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The restaurant culture in Barcelona, and Spain as a general, is very unique and I would recommend saving up for being able to visit as many as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Rather easy due to my prior language knowledge and due to the outgoing and friendly attitude of the locals. Even in instances where there was language difficulties, I always found that people were very patient and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to go up to strangers and talk to the, especially since they usually are just as interested in getting to know about your culture as you are about theirs. Often I experienced that they sometimes could be rather shy due to insecurities about their English abilities, but everyone would still try and put effort in, especially once you got to know them a bit.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Compared to northern Europe, the south has a very different time scheduling which took some getting used to intially.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the people, the openness and inclusiveness of the Catalan and Spanish people was much appreciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Patience with the administration, they were very unhelpful most of the time and you really have to be persistent if you want something done. Don't expect too much of the educational level, since it is very different to what you are used to. Be open to talking to strangers and other students as they can be extremely helpful with everything from administrative issues to daily life questions you may have.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to try out living in a different country and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to a completely different educational system than what you are used to took some time, and you don't know that your approach to learning needs to be different until it is usually too late. By this I mean that when you finally realize that you are focused on the wrong things in the teaching, it will most likely be halfway through the semester and by then you need to change your learning style completely. Adaptability is key.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
